A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseVOC work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and content relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original zero-shot and finetuning experiments on VidSTG and VLN, tracking comparisons, grounding evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds original BenSMOT finetuning results and pretraining/backbone ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the detection, association, greedy grouping, feature aggregation, captioning, and grounding procedures and training objectives. The smaller backbone appears as an additional experimental control.

E1.justification: V3 adds BenSMOT finetuning and evaluation, extending coverage to a dedicated person-tracking-and-captioning benchmark containing 3,292 videos (Sections 4.1 and 4.6). The existing pretraining datasets, VidSTG/VLN evaluations, and UVO experiment remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds direct comparisons with BeyondMOT (Li et al., 2024b) on BenSMOT and OW-VISCap on VidSTG in Tables 4–5. The OW-VISCap scores are explicitly attributed to the concurrent paper. Neither comparison appears in v2; the original tracking and grounding comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The new BenSMOT experiment reuses VidSTG finetuning hyperparameters, evaluates HOTA, DetA, AssA, and CIDEr, and includes settings without disjoint pretraining and with a smaller backbone. Existing benchmark splits, frame sampling, training budgets, and evaluation metrics are retained, including the relocated mAP-METEOR evaluation.

E4.justification: V3 Table 4 adds a focused ablation testing whether BenSMOT gains persist after removing disjoint pretraining and then reducing backbone capacity. The existing pretraining-mixture, frame-sampling, UVO, qualitative-error, and spatiotemporal-grounding analyses remain substantively unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experimental results.

E6.justification: New BenSMOT results report 90.19 HOTA and 0.254 CIDEr versus BeyondMOT's 71.98 and 0.087; removing pretraining and then reducing the backbone gives 88.56 and 86.55 HOTA. The new OW-VISCap comparison shows higher CHOTA for DenseVOC (56.9 versus 53.0), but lower CapA (39.7 versus 43.9). Matched original main-text and appendix result values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The association formulation, grounding rule, CHOTA definition, Algorithm 1, and expanded training-loss equations retain their mathematical content. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V3 adds a fifth introductory contribution claiming state-of-the-art semantic multi-object tracking on BenSMOT, including an 18.2-point HOTA advantage. The original task, architecture, disjoint-supervision, and grounding claims remain, and the abstract is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 adds interpretations concerning pretraining, backbone capacity, tracking architecture, and the language-model-size explanation for OW-VISCap's captioning advantage. Appendix D adds annotation subjectivity and the need for rigorous annotation protocols. Its single-caption limitation and richer-dataset future work already appeared in v2's conclusion.

D1.justification: V2 specifies JAX/Scenic and TPUs; v3 describes a public-GRiT-based implementation and GPUs, identifying V100s for pretraining while retaining reported budgets and timings. V3 also discloses the 46-million-parameter language head, revises CHOTA code-location instructions, and omits VLN captioned-trajectory counts. The PDFs do not explain the platform revision or establish reruns.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused positioning against BeyondMOT and OW-VISCap, distinguishing object coverage, tracking design, disjoint pretraining, and model size. V3 also adds LLaVA-OneVision, Cambrian-1, and OPT citations and removes the JAX/Scenic references. The broader related-work organization remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain. V3 condenses several introductory and experimental passages, adds a concurrent-work comparison subsection, updates the affiliation, and reorganizes the appendices into qualitative results, implementation, analyses, limitations, and broader impact.

P2.justification: The document receives a substantially different typographic and page layout. V2 Tables 3–4 are consolidated into v3 Table 3, with their mAP-METEOR columns redistributed into appendix Table 8. Figure 4 moves to the supplement, and new comparison Tables 4–5 are inserted. The existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: V3 Tables 4–5 strengthen comparative evidence through relevant concurrent methods, while the BenSMOT controls help distinguish architectural benefits from extra pretraining and backbone capacity. The OW-VISCap comparison also exposes a captioning tradeoff. These are useful additions to the unchanged core evidence, although brief BenSMOT protocol details and the unexplained hardware-description revision limit the reproducibility benefit.
